statement: Let \(\omega_1\) and \(\omega_2\) be two circles with centers \(C_1\) and \(C_2\), respectively, which intersect at two points \(P\) and \(Q\). Suppose that the circumcircle of triangle \(PC_1C_2\) intersects \(\omega_1\) at \(A \neq P\) and \(\omega_2\) at \(B \neq P\). Suppose further that \(Q\) is inside triangle \(PAB\). Show that \(Q\) is the incenter of triangle \(PAB\).

Given the real line with two marked points \(0\) and \(1\), we can perform the following operation as many times as desired: take two already marked points \(a\) and \(b\) and mark the reflection of \(a\) over \(b\). Let \(f(n)\) be the minimum number of operations needed to mark the integer \(n\) on the real line. For example, \(f(0) = f(1) = 0\) and \(f(-1) = f(2) = 1\). Find \(f(n)\).

Let \(\mathbb{R}_{>0}\) be the set of positive real numbers. Find all functions \(f : \mathbb{R}_{>0} \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}\) such that \[f(xy + f(x)) = f(f(x)f(y)) + x\] for all positive real numbers \(x\) and \(y\).

Prove that for every positive integer \(m\) there exists a positive integer \(n_m\) such that for every positive integer \(n \geq n_m\), there exist positive integers \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n\) such that \[\frac{1}{a_1^m} + \frac{1}{a_2^m} + \cdots + \frac{1}{a_n^m} = 1.\]

a) Prove that given constants \(a\), \(b\) with \(1 < a < 2 < b\), there is no partition of the set of positive integers into two subsets \(A_0\) and \(A_1\) such that: if \(j \in \{0,1\}\) and \(m, n\) are in \(A_j\), then either \(n/m < a\) or \(n/m > b\).

b) Find all pairs of real numbers \((a, b)\) with \(1 < a < 2 < b\) for which there exists a partition of the set of positive integers into three subsets \(A_0, A_1, A_2\) such that if \(j \in \{0,1,2\}\) and \(m, n\) are in \(A_j\), then either \(n/m < a\) or \(n/m > b\).

Let \(A_1A_2A_3A_4A_5\) be a convex cyclic pentagon with \(\angle A_i + \angle A_{i+1} > 180^\circ\) for all \(i \in \{1,2,3,4,5\}\) (all indices modulo \(5\)). Define \(B_i\) as the intersection of lines \(A_{i-1}A_i\) and \(A_{i+1}A_{i+2}\), forming a star. The circumcircles of triangles \(A_{i-1}B_{i-1}A_i\) and \(A_iB_iA_{i+1}\) meet again at \(C_i \neq A_i\), and the circumcircles of triangles \(B_{i-1}A_iB_i\) and \(B_iA_{i+1}B_{i+1}\) meet again at \(D_i \neq B_i\). Prove that the ten lines \(A_iC_i\), \(B_iD_i\), for \(i \in \{1,2,3,4,5\}\), have a common point.
